result.reason: Both items directly present the Rabbi Eliezer mishna challenge and the Gemara's explanation that his four cubits are subsumed (havlaat techumin), which is precisely what candidate 2's prose describes.

The passage directly quotes the exchange between Rabba bar bar Ḥana and Abaye about Rabbi Eliezer and the Rabbis' dispute being limited to devar reshut vs. devar mitzvah, which is precisely what the prose under heading 0 describes.

Both items present the Gemara's contradiction between the mishna's blanket return-home permission and the earlier two-thousand-amot limit, which is exactly what heading 1 ('Contradiction') describes — the question precedes Rav Yehuda's answer, which belongs under heading 2.

All four items together form the exact sequence described in the 'Rosh Hashanah Mishna' prose: the Gemara raises the Rosh Hashanah mishna difficulty (item 1), cites Rabban Gamliel's takana and the midwife/rescue cases (item 2), poses the contradiction about unlimited return (item 3), and gives Rav Yehuda's answer about weapons (item 4) — matching the candidate 1 prose precisely, which describes this entire chain including Rav Yehuda's answer as the resolution of the Rosh Hashanah mishna contradiction.

The passage describes the historical incident of soldiers being recognized by enemies, the ensuing chaos when retrieving weapons, and the resulting enactment — exactly what the 'Weapons Braita' prose section discusses in detail.

The passage directly presents Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak's resolution distinguishing between Jews defeating nations versus nations defeating Jews, which is precisely what the 'Rav Nachman' section prose describes.

Both items — Rav Yehuda/Rav's ruling on besieged towns and the baraita distinguishing monetary from life-threatening sieges — are explicitly discussed and paraphrased in the 'Siege Categories' prose, which is their clear and correct home.
Both items directly present the rule about border cities and Rav Nachman's application to Babylonia/Nehardea, which is precisely what the 'Border Cities' prose section discusses.

All four items discuss the Keilah episode — Rabbi Dostai's exposition, the baraita about the border city, and the Gemara's analysis of what David was asking God — which matches precisely the prose under 'David & Keilah'.

The passage is the mishna text itself, quoting Rabbi Meir's ruling about a person sitting on the road who unintentionally ends up near a city, which matches the 'Mishna Setup' prose that paraphrases exactly this scenario and ruling.

All three items constitute the Rabbi Tarfon narrative: the Mishnaic ruling, the baraita elaborating the story, and the Rabbis' rebuttal — exactly what the 'Rabbi Tarfon' prose section describes in detail.

All three items are the Mishnah about one who slept on the road without knowing Shabbat began, presenting Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri, the Rabbis, Rabbi Eliezer, and Rabbi Yehuda — exactly the content described in the 'Sleep Onset' prose.

Both items describe the case of two people whose four cubits partially overlap and the rule about eating in the middle but not carrying into each other's exclusive zone — exactly what the 'Two People' prose discusses.

Both items deal with the three-person overlapping techum case and Rabbi Shimon's courtyard analogy illustrating it — they belong together under 'Three People' (index 0), not under 'Three Courtyards' (index 1), since the courtyard analogy is introduced as an illustration of the three-person scenario, and the 'Three People' prose already references the middle person being 'swallowed between them' which is the exact content of item 1, while item 2 is Rabbi Shimon's analogy for that same case.

All three items are Rava's dilemma about Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri's position — whether ownerless objects acquire shevita or not — which is precisely what the 'Cheftzei Hefker' prose describes in detail.

All four items — Rav Yosef's rain baraita, the analysis of whose opinion it reflects regarding hefker acquiring residence, and Rav Safra's challenge about rain near a city — are precisely the content described in the 'Rain Case' prose.
The passage quotes the mishna about cisterns (bor shel yachid, shel ota ha'ir, shel olei Bavel) which is precisely the content described in the 'Wells Case' prose section.

Both items together present the contradiction between the two braitot and its resolution (ha Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri, ha Rabbanan), which is precisely what the 'Mapping Debate' prose describes as its central content.
